output.answer_markdown: Iron Mountain describes several strategies for managing foreign currency risk. One is to finance certain international subsidiaries with local-currency debt as a natural hedge [1]. Another is for IMI or IMIM to borrow in foreign currencies to hedge intercompany financing [2]. On occasion it uses currency swaps to hedge an overseas investment [3]. It has also entered into cross-currency swap agreements to hedge dollar-euro exchange rate variability [4]. It may use foreign-currency borrowings to hedge its international investments [5].

provenance.quote: One strategy is to finance certain of our international subsidiaries with debt that is denominated in local currencies, thereby providing a natural hedge.

claims.text: Iron Mountain finances certain of its international subsidiaries with debt denominated in local currencies, which provides a natural hedge.

provenance.quote: Another strategy we utilize is for IMI or IMIM, a wholly-owned subsidiary of IMI, to borrow in foreign currencies to hedge our intercompany financing activities.

claims.text: IMI or IMIM, a wholly-owned subsidiary of IMI, borrows in foreign currencies to hedge intercompany financing activities.

provenance.quote: on occasion, we enter into currency swaps to temporarily or permanently hedge an overseas investment, such as a major acquisition, to lock in certain transaction economics.

claims.text: On occasion, Iron Mountain enters into currency swaps to temporarily or permanently hedge an overseas investment.

provenance.quote: We have entered into cross-currency swap agreements to hedge the variability of exchange rate impacts between the United States dollar and the Euro.

claims.text: Iron Mountain has entered into cross-currency swap agreements to hedge the variability of exchange rate impacts between the United States dollar and the Euro.

provenance.quote: We may also use borrowings in foreign currencies, either obtained in the United States or by our foreign subsidiaries, to hedge foreign currency risk associated with our international investments.

claims.text: Iron Mountain may use borrowings in foreign currencies, obtained in the United States or by its foreign subsidiaries, to hedge foreign currency risk associated with its international investments.
